name: Old Fashioned
description: Spirit, sugar, bitters, and a citrus twist—the template for countless whiskey drinks.
history: One of the earliest cocktail templates, the Old Fashioned asks for whiskey sweetened lightly and lifted with aromatic bitters. It remains the bar’s clearest proof that restraint beats complexity.
whyItWorks: Sugar softens whiskey’s edges while bitters add spice and depth; the orange oils perfume the glass without turning the drink into a fruit cocktail.

ingredients.label: Demerara sugar or ¼ oz rich simple

steps: Add sugar and bitters to a rocks glass. Muddle briefly with a splash of water, or stir until dissolved.
Add bourbon and a large ice cube.
Stir until chilled and lightly diluted, about 20–30 seconds.
Express an orange peel over the drink and drop it in. Add a cherry only if you like a soft finish.
techniqueNotes: Prefer a large ice cube so dilution stays controlled.
Rye makes a spicier, drier Old Fashioned; wheated or toasted bourbons read sweeter and richer.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Classic, balanced, and oak-forward—ideal for the standard build.
Polished with extra oak influence; elegant and structured.
Softer and fruitier; a gentler evening pour.
Richer and sweeter from the toasted finish—great when you want dessert-adjacent warmth.

substitutions.notes: Sazerac Rye or Elijah Craig Rye for a spicier profile.
Use about ¼ oz simple syrup if you prefer no muddling.
